title: 10 factors: healing after periapical surgery
topic: Ten factors a Cohen's chapter links to periapical healing after periapical surgery: 7 from pooled data, 3 from individual studies.

claims.claim: Lesion size: ≤5 mm vs >5 mm — small side associated with better healing
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp 12e, ch. 17 — unpublished pooled meta-analysis cited by the chapter (ref. 130, unpublished manuscript 2014); chapter RR 1.2 (95% CI 1.1, 1.3)

claims.claim: Cortical plates: one involved vs both — one-plate side associated with better healing
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp 12e, ch. 17 — unpublished pooled meta-analysis cited by the chapter (ref. 130, unpublished manuscript 2014); chapter RR 1.2 (95% CI 1.0, 1.5)

claims.claim: Previous surgery: absent vs present — absent associated with better healing
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp 12e, ch. 17 — unpublished pooled meta-analysis cited by the chapter (ref. 130, unpublished manuscript 2014); chapter RR 1.2 (95% CI 1.1, 1.3)

claims.claim: Magnification: used vs not used — used associated with better healing
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp 12e, ch. 17 — unpublished pooled meta-analysis cited by the chapter (ref. 130, unpublished manuscript 2014); chapter RR 1.5 (95% CI 1.3, 1.8)

claims.claim: Root-end bevel: minimum vs obvious — minimum associated with better healing
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp 12e, ch. 17 — unpublished pooled meta-analysis cited by the chapter (ref. 130, unpublished manuscript 2014); chapter RR 1.3 (95% CI 1.2, 1.4)

claims.claim: Retro-cavity prep: ultrasonic tip vs bur — ultrasonic tip associated with better healing
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp 12e, ch. 17 — unpublished pooled meta-analysis cited by the chapter (ref. 130, unpublished manuscript 2014); chapter RR 1.3 (95% CI 1.2, 1.4)

claims.claim: Retro-filling: MTA, SuperEBA or IRM vs amalgam; MTA: similar outcome to SuperEBA or IRM
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp 12e, ch. 17 — unpublished pooled meta-analysis cited by the chapter (ref. 130, unpublished manuscript 2014). The chapter lists MTA, SuperEBA or IRM versus amalgam; its RR against amalgam is for SuperEBA and IRM, 1.2 (1.1, 1.3); MTA vs SuperEBA 1.0 (0.99, 1.1); MTA vs IRM 1.1 (0.98, 1.1)

claims.claim: Pre-op signs or symptoms: absent vs present (univariate only) — absent associated with better healing
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp 12e, ch. 17 names the factor (RR 1.2; 95% CI 1.1, 1.3) citing Villa-Machado et al., Int Endod J 2013;46:1063-76 (PMID 23560363). The chapter does not state the favored side; it is taken from the study's PubMed abstract, where the association was univariate and not independent after multivariate regression (abstract only read)

claims.claim: Periodontal status: endo-only lesion vs endo-perio — isolated endodontic lesion associated with better healing
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp 12e, ch. 17 names the factor (RR 2.1; 95% CI 1.1, 3.8) citing Song et al., J Endod 2013;39:1491-7 (PMID 24238435). The chapter does not state the favored side or the categories; they are taken from the study's PubMed abstract: isolated endodontic lesion vs endodontic-periodontal lesion (abstract only read)

claims.claim: Coronal restoration: satisfactory vs unsatisfactory — satisfactory associated with better healing
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp 12e, ch. 17 names the factor (RR 1.6; 95% CI 1.2, 2.1) citing Villa-Machado et al., Int Endod J 2013;46:1063-76 (PMID 23560363). The chapter does not state the favored side; it is taken from the study's PubMed abstract, where unsatisfactory coronal restoration stayed independently associated with a worse outcome (abstract only read)

caption:
Ten pins, ten factors associated with better periapical healing after periapical surgery.

A study summary of the Evaluation of Outcomes chapter in Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp, for teeth with a preoperative periapical radiolucency.
Back 7 = the chapter's unpublished pooled analysis. Front 3 = individual studies: the chapter names them, the favored side is from the cited studies.
Signs or symptoms: univariate only in Villa-Machado 2013.
Periapical healing, not tooth survival. Associations, not causation.

Refs: Ng & Gulabivala, Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp 12e, ch. 17; Villa-Machado 2013, Int Endod J; Song 2013, J Endod.
